# Shared literature and citation verification

Use one source record for novelty, missing baselines, and bibliography repair. Reuse verified records across phases; revisit when the paper version or substantive claim changes.

## Two distinct checks

1. **Identity:** Does the work exist, and are title, authors, year, version, venue/status, and supplied DOI correct?
2. **Support:** Does its actual method/result support the manuscript sentence or review criticism under comparable assumptions and evaluation conditions?

A metadata match establishes identity, not scientific support. An existing paper can be cited inaccurately.

## Source workflow

- Search published titles, public method names, or technical concepts. Inspect the original paper, official proceedings, publisher record, or author manuscript. Crossref, DBLP, arXiv, and other indexes can resolve metadata and versions.
- Separate preprint and proceedings versions. Do not combine a title from one version with an incompatible year, author list, or DOI from another.
- Read the passage, equation, or result used to justify a material claim. Record URL/identifier and location. Snippets and abstracts usually cannot establish method equivalence or benchmark comparability.
- Fetch BibTeX or citation metadata from an authoritative record when an edit requires it. Never fill a missing DOI, page range, author, or venue from memory.
- If access fails, retain the entry as unverified or partially verified. Failure to find a record is not proof of fabrication. Explain which fields or support claims remain unresolved.

For a full audit, check cited-work identity when feasible and prioritize full-text support verification for central claims and suspected mismatches. Report actual coverage, including entries checked versus total and claims given full-text checks. Never call a sampled check a complete bibliography audit.

Check citation keys against actual bibliography files and build: missing keys, unresolved citations, duplicate records, and malformed metadata. Unused BibTeX records are usually cleanup. A local syntax check cannot establish reference existence.

## Works cited by the review

Limit the review's references to works supporting an actual assessment. Cite verified primary sources and mark version differences. If a reference cannot be verified, retain it as a lead in evidence notes; remove or qualify dependent criticism. Do not leave an unsupported novelty accusation after deleting its citation.

During audit-only work, record suspected corrections rather than editing `.bib` files or inserting fake keys. During authorized revisions, apply verified corrections and flag unresolved sources outside the manuscript or as disclosed comments when requested.

If browsing is unavailable or prohibited, use supplied papers and authoritative records, label supplied-source verification, and leave current literature coverage unresolved. Do not simulate a search from memory.
